name: Netherlands
summary: Amsterdam claims the oldest stock exchange in the world: the Dutch East India Company (VOC) was the first company on it, in 1602. Today Euronext Amsterdam's AEX tracks 30 large companies, led by a few global names in semiconductors, energy, consumer goods and finance.

currency.name: Euro
currency.note: Same currency as Austria, so no exchange-rate risk for a euro investor. Several AEX companies report in other currencies or earn most of their revenue abroad.

source.title: FTSE Equity Country Classification Process, v3.5, October 2026, Appendix 3 (FTSE Russell, PDF)

exchanges.name: Euronext Amsterdam
exchanges.founded: 1602 (Euronext calls it the oldest stock exchange in the world); part of Euronext since 2000
exchanges.hours: Runs on Euronext's single trading platform: an opening auction, continuous trading through the European business day and a closing auction. Euronext publishes the exact phase times in its trading manual; this site has not verified them separately for Amsterdam.
exchanges.note: Amsterdam follows the Euronext holiday calendar; in 2026 it trades on Ascension Day and Whit Monday.

indexes.name: AEX
indexes.description: The 30 largest and most actively traded shares on Euronext Amsterdam, weighted by free-float market capitalisation. History since 1 March 1983. The ten largest members made up about 77% of the index at the end of September 2026.

source.title: AEX-Index factsheet as of 30 September 2026 (Euronext, PDF)

regulators.name: Dutch Authority for the Financial Markets (AFM)
regulators.role: Supervises the conduct of the entire financial market sector since 1 March 2002, including capital markets, investment firms and financial reporting.

regulators.name: De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB)
regulators.role: Central bank and prudential supervisor; it administers the Dutch deposit guarantee.

investorProtection.name: Dutch deposit guarantee
investorProtection.text: Money in bank accounts is automatically protected up to €100,000 per person and bank. Investment products such as shares and bonds are not covered by it.

settlement.cycle: T+2 (two business days); T+1 from 11 October 2027
settlement.csd: Euroclear Nederland (one of Euroclear's ESES CSDs)
settlement.note: Like the rest of the EU, the Netherlands moves to next-day settlement on 11 October 2027.

source.title: One year to go for T+1 settlement (ESMA, 16 October 2026)

rules.title: Short selling (EU rules)
rules.text: Net short positions in shares must be reported to the regulator from 0.1% of issued share capital and published from 0.5% (Category N).

rules.title: High concentration
rules.text: The AEX is dominated by a handful of companies: at the end of September 2026, the largest member alone had a weight of about 17%.

source.title: AEX-Index factsheet as of 30 September 2026 (Euronext, PDF)

taxes.glance: 15% Dutch dividend tax withheld by the paying company; foreign investors may claim relief under a tax treaty. Dutch residents are taxed under their own income tax system (not covered here).

items.title: Dividend tax
items.text: The general rate of Dutch dividend tax is 15%, withheld by the company paying the dividend.

items.title: For an Austrian investor
items.text: An Austrian bank can credit foreign withholding tax up to 15% of the dividend against Austrian KESt (Category Q), which matches the Dutch rate.

items.title: Residents
items.text: Dutch residents are taxed on savings and investments under the Dutch income tax system, which is complex and being reformed; check the Dutch Tax and Customs Administration.

access: Many Austrian banks and brokers offer trading on Euronext Amsterdam in euros.
Indirectly, through funds or ETFs on the AEX or broader European indexes (Category H).

history.text: The Dutch East India Company (VOC) is the first company on the Amsterdam exchange.
Start of the AEX index history (1 March).
The Amsterdam, Brussels and Paris exchanges combine to form Euronext.
The Amsterdam exchange celebrates its 417th anniversary.

funFacts: At the end of September 2026, the ten largest AEX members made up about 77% of the index, more than in the DAX (about 65%) or the CAC 40 (about 62%).

sources.title: ESES CSDs: Euroclear Belgium, Euroclear France, Euroclear Nederland (Euroclear)
